sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and shared names
sections.what: Loads the configuration from the core module and sets the reasoning file name and the list of columns that must hold JSON.
sections.why: The reasoning file name is copied here because importing the design system module would cause a loop.
sections.watch_out: The reasoning file name is copied, so renaming it in the design system module means changing it here too.

sections.name: _read_rows
sections.title: Reads a CSV file
sections.what: Opens a CSV file as UTF-8 and returns its column names and all of its rows.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: every check needs the column names and rows from the same read.
sections.watch_out: Files that are not UTF-8 raise an error, which the caller catches and reports.

sections.name: _check_file
sections.title: Checks one data file
sections.what: Reports a file that is missing or cannot be read. Confirms that the expected columns exist. Looks for repeated ID numbers in files that have a 'No' column. Warns about stack files that lack that column. Checks that JSON columns contain valid JSON.
sections.why: Each check targets a way the search output could break or give wrong answers.
sections.watch_out: Empty ID values are treated as duplicates when more than one row is empty.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Runs all checks and reports
sections.what: Runs the file check on every domain file, every stack file, and the reasoning file. Collects every problem. Prints them all and exits with failure, or prints an OK line and exits successfully.
sections.why: Gives one complete list so a single run shows every broken file.
sections.watch_out: The docstring says a successful run prints nothing, but the code prints an OK message, so the documentation is out of date.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Runs main when started directly
sections.what: Calls the main routine only when this file is run as a program, not when it is imported.
sections.why: Lets other code import the checks without starting them.

summary: Checks that every design data file has the expected columns, no repeated ID numbers, and valid JSON, then reports all problems at once.
purpose: Catches broken or inconsistent data before it is published or released.
why: The file docstring says a data change can break several files at once, so it collects every problem in one run instead of stopping at the first.
how: Read the configuration of every domain and stack file. For each one, check it exists, can be read, has the expected columns, has no repeated ID numbers, and has valid JSON in the decision rules column. Check the reasoning file the same way. Print all problems and exit with failure, or print an OK line and exit successfully.
inputs: The configured data folder and the CSV files inside it.
outputs: A success message or a list of problems with the exit code set to fail or success.
risks: A missing file is reported but other checks still run, so a long list may hide the one real cause.
debug: Run the script and read the problem list, which names the file and row. For a JSON problem, check the named row. For a missing column, compare the header row with the config.
